entries.meta: A hardware enclave inside a CPU or GPU designed to isolate running code and memory from the machine's owner and operating system, while signing cryptographic reports of the binary loaded inside it.

entries.meta: A one-time ceremony required by some polynomial commitment schemes to generate public parameters from secret random numbers that must subsequently be destroyed ("toxic waste").

entries.meta: Confirming a claim against evidence that holds up even when the party making the claim has an incentive to cheat.
entries.name: Verification

entries.meta: The lightweight program that inspects a cryptographic proof and outputs accept or refuse.
entries.name: Verifier
entries.terms: verifier the lightweight program that inspects a cryptographic proof and outputs accept or refuse.

entries.meta: The learned numerical parameters that define a trained neural network, numbering in the billions for modern language models.

entries.meta: All the private inputs and intermediate values that the prover knows and uses to construct a proof, which the verifier does not see directly.
